answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to post a small, time-locked stake that matures only after sustained useful work, like a vine that must climb before it bears fruit. Newcomers start with a narrow trust quota; each verified transaction adds reputation, and a peer review can flag an opal of doubt - a suspicious pattern - freezing the stake until an independent check clears it. Forging thousands of identities on a flat mesa of equal cost per fake scales linearly in cost, while honest agents compound reputation, so mass fakery is uneconomic.
